title: ARWP GitHub Pages Search Pack
purpose: Prove GitHub Pages host identity, publication boundaries and project-subpath Search integrity without confusing repository hints, a CNAME file, a successful workflow or optional Google acquisition features with deployed Search outcomes.

rules.claim: A GitHub Pages user/organization site, a repository project subpath and a custom-domain site have different public-root contracts.
rules.decision: Classify the supplied public site against owner/repository identity; fail contradictory github.io paths or custom-domain site roots with an unexpected subdirectory.

rules.claim: GitHub Pages can publish from a branch or a custom Actions artifact; repository files alone do not prove what was deployed.
rules.decision: Require an explicit publication mode, retain missing/custom-workflow evidence as watch, and require final artifact evidence before release completeness.

rules.claim: Branch publishing uses Jekyll by default unless the publishing source contains .nojekyll; non-Jekyll generators are better represented by custom Actions or an explicit .nojekyll publication source.
rules.decision: Classify branch source as Jekyll-default or nojekyll without guessing the generator; warn when a source looks prebuilt/non-Jekyll but neither boundary is explicit.

rules.claim: A project site under owner.github.io/repository/ must keep its Search-owned URLs inside that project base path.
rules.decision: Use the final artifact Search Build Gate for canonical/sitemap identity, fail feed/robots Search references that escape the project root, and watch ordinary root-relative navigation/assets that may intentionally depend on a host-root resource.

rules.claim: A repository CNAME file is a source declaration, not proof that GitHub Pages currently serves that custom domain.
rules.decision: Fail a source CNAME that contradicts the supplied custom-domain host; keep a missing CNAME/settings proof as watch and require HTTPS for release-facing custom-domain evidence.

rules.claim: Google Preferred Sources accepts domain/subdomain sites but not a project subdirectory as an independently selectable source.
rules.decision: Delegate hostname-scope applicability to Search Platform Eligibility: github.io project sites are subdirectory/not-applicable; hostname-root and custom-domain roots are scope-eligible but not guaranteed to appear in the feature.

rules.claim: A green Pages deployment is revision-specific evidence and must be followed by final live parity for the same source revision.
rules.decision: Leave exact deployment SHA and live HTML parity to Production Search Build Gate; this pack reports release evidence incomplete until final artifact proof exists and never treats source-only checks as deployment proof.
